plans.objective: [DIM: composition] The rigid polynomial family exhibits a low-dimensional solution space where the minimum width $N_c$ required to generalize to held-out points remains flat or decreasing with increasing constraint count $w$, while the fat polynomial family exhibits $N_c = \infty$ (unreachable) within the scan range due to high-dimensional oscillatory behavior.

steps.description: Implement the family(kind, w, seed) function for the rigid (linear f(x)=x) and fat (high-oscillation polynomial f(x)=(2x-1)^19) polynomial families, ensuring outputs are normalized to O(1) scale, Xv/X are non-overlapping, and y/yv have shape (N,1). This will enable the capacity_scan to properly evaluate N_c(w) trends for both families.

plans.objective: [DIM: structure] The rigid polynomial family exhibits a finite critical width $N_c$ that is invariant with respect to the number of training constraints $w$, indicating a low-dimensional solution space where the network capacity is determined by the intrinsic dimensionality of the function class rather than the data density.

steps.description: [auto-routed: surprise=1.00] Implement the `family(kind, w, seed)` function that generates training and held-out constraint points for two function classes: (1) rigid family (linear function f(x)=x, low-dimensional solution space) and (2) fat family (high-oscillation polynomial f(x)=(2x-1)^19, high-dimensional). Ensure y and yv are normalized to O(1) scale by dividing by std, shapes are (N,1), and held-out points Xv do not overlap with training points X. This addresses the missing anchor data and enables the capacity scan to determine N_c(w).
